category_title: Students who exhibit initial fear and avoidance but transition to engagement through curiosity and hands-on success
minimal_context: The student is participating in a group nature walk in the woods to look for bugs and observe worms under an overturned log.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Alright everyone, we are going into the woods now for our nature walk to look for bugs.

STUDENT: (Zips up her sweatshirt and ties her hood on tight) I am very scared about going into the woods. I don't like bugs.

TUTOR: Just keep walking with the group.

STUDENT: (Holds her field guide over her head) This isn't something that I want to do. I'm scared.

TUTOR: Everyone step off the path over here. There are a lot of worms under this overturned log to look at.

STUDENT: (Refuses to walk toward the overturned logs) Why does it have to be over there?

options.A: Provide the student with specific science vocabulary, such as biotic and abiotic, associated with the bugs and worms.
options.B: Probe the student to consider multiple plausible answers about the bugs, deliberately stepping back from being the single source of knowledge.
options.C: Ask the student what they think went wrong during the nature walk instead of telling them what went wrong.
options.D: Organize group work, social interaction, and hands-on activities during the nature walk while providing scaffolding or external support.
